chapter: Glen Island, early records and Duke Ellington
title: Playing Ellington-style arrangements by Andy Gibson, and Tizol's tunes
summary: Around 1937 Barnet's band took up Ellington voicings through arranger Andy Gibson, and Juan Tizol brought tunes to rehearsals.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Great. So at some point you began playing Ellington -- your band began playing Ellington music. At what point was that?

Oh, that was along around 1937 there. And I got the guys in the band, I said, "Who can I get who can write me some of this stuff?" You know. And so they got me together with a guy by the name of Andy Gibson. And Andy started writing for us, and of course he was very much influenced by the Ellington voicings and the Ellington sound and we got a whole bunch of his arrangements in, and Tizol, you know, was always, he was writing tunes, you know. He'd already done, "Caravan", and "Azure", and he was always giving us tunes. He used to come up to our rehearsals. He took quite an interest in our band at that time. I think he felt he was getting the wrong end of the stick from Mills in that thing, because he wrote "Caravan", and the only thing that -- I can't imagine what Irving Mills had to do with that.
